questions.question: That charge is QUANTISED means:
options: Charge exists only in whole-number multiples of the fundamental charge 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C
Charge can take any value at all

questions.question: A sphere carries −4,8 × 10⁻¹⁷ C. The number of excess electrons is:
An object that has LOST 5 × 10¹⁰ electrons carries a charge of:
options: +8 × 10⁻⁹ C — losing electrons leaves a proton surplus, so the charge is positive

questions.question: One nanocoulomb (nC) equals:

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Charge an Object

questions.question: In every charging process, the particles that actually move are:
options: Electrons only — protons are locked in nuclei and never transfer

questions.question: Touching a negatively charged rod to a neutral metal sphere leaves the sphere:
options: Negatively charged — charging by contact gives both objects the SAME sign
Charged only on the far side

questions.question: In charging by induction, a negatively charged rod is brought near a metal sphere, the far side is earthed, the earth is removed and then the rod is removed. The sphere is left:
options: POSITIVELY charged — the repelled electrons ran off to earth, leaving a proton surplus
Charged only while the rod is present

questions.question: A charged ruler attracts small neutral scraps of paper because:
options: The paper is also charged by friction
The paper's molecules become POLARISED — the electron clouds shift so the near side carries the opposite charge

subtopics.title: Conservation of Charge and the Sharing Rule

questions.question: The principle of conservation of charge states that:
options: Charge cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred — the total charge of an isolated system is unchanged
Charge always becomes zero after contact
Positive charge is conserved but negative charge is not
Charge can be created by rubbing

questions.question: Identical spheres carrying +5 nC and −3 nC touch and separate. Each then carries:
In that transfer, sphere A went from +5 nC to +1 nC. The number of electrons it gained is:
The halving rule Q = (Q₁ + Q₂) ÷ 2 may only be used when:
options: The two conducting spheres are IDENTICAL, and the charges are added with their signs

subtopics.title: Coulomb's Law and the Inverse Square

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the electrostatic force between two point charges is:
options: Directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
Directly proportional to the distance between them
Inversely proportional to the product of the charges

questions.question: Charges of +3 × 10⁻⁶ C and −4 × 10⁻⁶ C sit 0,30 m apart. The force is:
Those same charges are moved to 0,60 m apart. The force becomes:
options: 0,3 N — a QUARTER of the original, because the distance is squared

questions.question: Why should the negative sign of a charge NOT be substituted into F = kQ₁Q₂ ÷ r²?
options: Because r cannot be squared then
Because the answer would be in coulombs
Because it produces a meaningless negative force — substitute magnitudes, then state attraction or repulsion in words

subtopics.title: The Balloon and the School Jersey

questions.question: Rubbing a balloon on a jersey leaves the balloon negative because:
options: Electrons were scraped off the jersey onto the balloon — only the negative bits ever move
Protons moved from the jersey to the balloon
New charge was created by the rubbing

questions.question: The charged balloon sticks to an uncharged wall because:
options: The balloon's negatives push the wall's negatives away from the surface, leaving the wall's face slightly positive, and opposites attract

questions.question: Saying charge is 'counted in whole electrons, never half of one' is the plain-language version of:

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Get Charged, and Sharing the Total

questions.question: A doorknob 'bites' you in dry winter weather because:
options: You picked up extra electrons walking across the floor, and the metal knob is the first easy escape route they find
The metal is colder than your hand
The knob was charged by induction

questions.question: Holding a negative rod near a metal ball, earthing the far side, then removing finger and rod, leaves the ball:
options: Negative, the same as the rod
Positive — the opposite of what was brought near, because the crowded electrons ran away through your finger

questions.question: Identical balls of +5 and −3 touching and separating give each ball:
options: +1 each — add the signs first, giving +2, then share it out

questions.question: Adding 5 and 3 as sizes rather than adding +5 and −3 with signs is wrong because:
options: The answer would be in coulombs
It would mean charge appeared out of nowhere, and charge is never created

questions.question: Moving two charges three times as far apart changes the force to:
options: One ninth of what it was
One third of what it was

questions.question: Why must 30 cm be turned into 0,30 m before anything else?
options: Because that number is about to be squared, so a slip there is a slip of ten thousand times
Because forces are measured in centimetres

questions.question: In the worked example, dividing 0,108 by 0,09 gives:
The two habits that carry every Coulomb's law calculation are:
options: Skip the formula, and answer in coulombs
Add the charges, then divide by two
Convert to metres before squaring, and leave the signs out of the sum — then state attraction or repulsion in words
